tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

10	
11	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
12	
13	### User Story 1 - Returning user logs in (Priority: P1)
14	
15	A person who already has a Cerne account opens the app, enters their email and password on the login screen, and reaches the main conversation screen (Home/Chat).
16	
17	**Why this priority**: Nothing else in the product — capture, chat, records, settings — is reachable without this. It is the single gate every other unit depends on.
18	
19	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by submitting valid credentials on the login screen and confirming the app lands on Home/Chat; delivers a working, demonstrable access path on its own.
20	
21	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
22	
23	1. **Given** a user with a valid existing account and no active session, **When** they enter the correct email and password on the login screen and submit, **Then** they are authenticated and taken to the Home/Chat screen.
24	2. **Given** a user on the login screen, **When** they submit incorrect credentials, **Then** they see a clear, non-crashing error message and remain on the login screen able to retry.
25	3. **Given** a user with no network connection, **When** they submit the login form, **Then** they see a retryable connection-error message rather than the app hanging or crashing.
26	
27	---
28	
29	### User Story 2 - New user creates an account (Priority: P2)
30	
31	A person without a Cerne account switches the same screen to sign-up mode, enters an email and password, and reaches Home/Chat as a newly created user.
32	
33	**Why this priority**: Required for anyone without an account to enter the product at all, but it depends on the same screen and session machinery as login, so it is one step below it.
34	
35	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by toggling to "Criar conta", submitting a new email/password pair, and confirming an account is created and the app lands on Home/Chat.
36	
37	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
38	
39	1. **Given** a person without an account, **When** they switch to "Criar conta" mode, enter a new email and password, and submit, **Then** an account is created and they are taken directly to Home/Chat.
40	2. **Given** a person entering an email that is already registered, **When** they submit the sign-up form, **Then** they see a clear error message and can correct and retry without the app crashing.
41	
42	---
43	
44	### User Story 3 - App launches and routes by session state (Priority: P3)
45	
46	Whenever the app is opened, it shows a brief splash state, checks whether a usable session already exists, and sends the user straight to Home/Chat or to the login/sign-up screen accordingly — without ever leaving them stuck on the splash screen.
47	
48	**Why this priority**: Determines where every single app session begins; it depends on User Story 1 existing but is a thin routing layer on top of it rather than new user-facing capability.
49	
50	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by launching the app under three stored-session conditions (valid, expired-but-refreshable, none) and confirming the correct landing screen each time.
51	
52	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
53	
54	1. **Given** a device with a previously stored, still-valid session, **When** the app is launched, **Then** after the splash state the user lands directly on Home/Chat without re-entering credentials.
55	2. **Given** a device with no stored session (first launch, or after logout), **When** the app is launched, **Then** after the splash state the user lands on the login/sign-up screen.
56	3. **Given** a device with an expired-but-refreshable session, **When** the app is launched, **Then** the app renews the session in the background and lands on Home/Chat without prompting the user.
57	
58	---
59	
60	### User Story 4 - Navigating between the main screens (Priority: P4)
61	
62	From Home/Chat, the user opens the side menu and moves to Meus Registros or Configurações (today, placeholders), and back, without losing their place.
63	
64	**Why this priority**: Establishes the skeleton every later unit (RF06/RF07/RF05, RF09, etc.) will fill in; it has no functional payload yet, so it ranks below the screens that actually unlock product value.
65	
66	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the side menu from Home/Chat, visiting each destination, and returning, confirming Home/Chat's state is unchanged.
67	
68	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
69	
70	1. **Given** the user is on Home/Chat, **When** they open the side menu and select "Meus Registros", **Then** they see the Meus Registros placeholder screen and can return to Home/Chat.
71	2. **Given** the user is on Home/Chat, **When** they open the side menu and select "Configurações", **Then** they see the Configurações placeholder screen and can return to Home/Chat.
72	3. **Given** the user is on any main screen, **When** they open the side menu, **Then** the menu overlays the current screen without discarding the state underneath it.
73	
74	---
75	
76	### User Story 5 - Session expires during active use (Priority: P5)
77	
78	While the user is actively on a screen (e.g., scrolled partway through Home/Chat), the backend session expires; an overlay appears explaining this and offering to log in again, and once they do, they return to exactly where they were.
79	
80	**Why this priority**: An edge condition of an already-working session (Story 1); important for trust and data safety, but it cannot be exercised until login and at least one screen exist.
81	
82	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a session-expired response while a screen is in a known state, confirming the overlay appears over it unchanged, and confirming re-authentication restores that exact state.
83	
84	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
85	
86	1. **Given** the user is actively viewing a screen in a particular state (e.g., a given scroll position), **When** the backend reports the session has expired, **Then** a "Sessão expirada" overlay appears on top of the current screen without resetting its state.
87	2. **Given** the "Sessão expirada" overlay is visible, **When** the user taps "Entrar novamente" and re-authenticates successfully, **Then** the overlay is dismissed and the underlying screen is restored exactly as it was.
88	
89	---
90	
91	### Edge Cases
92	
93	- Submitting the login or sign-up form with an empty field shows an inline validation message immediately, with no network call made.
94	- The backend rejects a login or sign-up submission as malformed (non-retryable) — this is shown and handled distinctly from a timeout or offline condition (retryable).
95	- The stored access token is present but its refresh token is itself invalid or expired at launch — the user is routed to the login screen, never left stuck on the splash state.
96	- The session expires a second time while the user is still dismissing a "Sessão expirada" overlay from the first expiration — the overlay persists/reappears rather than letting the user proceed with a stale session.
97	- A user opens a placeholder screen (Meus Registros, Configurações) before its owning unit is built — it renders cleanly as "not yet available" rather than a blank or broken screen.
98	- The app is backgrounded mid-submission of login or sign-up — on resume, the request either completes normally or fails cleanly, and never results in a duplicate account or a duplicate session.
99	
100	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
101	
102	### Functional Requirements
103	
104	- **FR-001**: The project MUST be organized so that every feature added from this unit onward follows one fixed folder convention, so later units have a single place to add their own code without restructuring the foundation.
105	- **FR-002**: The system MUST define every visual value (color, typography, spacing, corner radius) used anywhere in the app in exactly one central place; no screen delivered by this unit may define a visual value anywhere else.
106	- **FR-003**: The system MUST provide a single way for any feature to call the backend that always yields either a success result or a typed failure — never an unhandled crash.
107	- **FR-004**: The system MUST translate every backend error response's error code, message, and retryable flag into a failure the UI can act on, so screens can tell a retryable problem (e.g., timeout) from one that is not (e.g., invalid credentials).
108	- **FR-005**: The system MUST address the backend using the documented real request path for each operation, not the contract's documentation-only path.
109	- **FR-006**: Users MUST be able to create a new account by submitting an email and password from the sign-up mode of the login screen.
110	- **FR-007**: Users MUST be able to authenticate with an existing email and password from the login mode of the same screen.
111	- **FR-008**: Users MUST be able to toggle between login and sign-up mode on the same screen without being sent to a different screen.
112	- **FR-009**: The system MUST check, on every app launch, whether a usable session already exists — renewing it first if it is merely expired-but-renewable — and route the user to Home/Chat when one exists or to the login screen otherwise.
113	- **FR-010**: The system MUST show a splash state while this session check (and any related background preparation) is in progress, before routing the user anywhere.
114	- **FR-011**: Users MUST be able to reach Home/Chat, Meus Registros, and Configurações from a side menu, and return to Home/Chat from either of them.
115	- **FR-012**: Meus Registros and Configurações MUST appear as clearly-labeled placeholder screens with no functional behavior from later requirements (RF01–RF10), reserving space for the units that will fill them in.
116	- **FR-013**: The system MUST show a "Sessão expirada" overlay on top of whatever screen the user is on when the backend reports the session has expired, without discarding that screen's state underneath.
117	- **FR-014**: Users MUST be able to dismiss the "Sessão expirada" overlay by re-authenticating, after which the screen underneath MUST be restored to its prior state.
118	- **FR-015**: The system MUST present a clear, non-crashing message for every error condition that sign-up, login, session-renewal, or session-check can return.
119	- **FR-016**: This unit MUST NOT implement the functional behavior of any RF01–RF10 requirement; any screen or control belonging to one of them MUST exist only as an inert placeholder, if at all.
120	- **FR-017**: This unit MUST NOT modify the backend, its contract, or its configuration in any way.
121	
122	### Key Entities
123	
124	- **Session**: Represents whether the user is currently authenticated — holds the information needed to stay logged in and to know when it has expired or can be silently renewed. Determines whether a launch routes to Home/Chat or to the login screen, and whether an active screen receives the "Sessão expirada" overlay.
125	- **Account**: The identity a person signs up with or logs into — an email address and the credential tied to it.
126	- **Backend Failure**: The error outcome every call introduced by this unit (sign-up, login, refresh, session check) can produce — carries enough information to distinguish a retryable problem from a non-retryable one, and to choose the message shown to the user.
127	- **Placeholder Destination**: A navigable screen (Meus Registros, Configurações) that exists so later units have somewhere to add their functionality, but carries no behavior of its own in this unit.
128	
129	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
130	
131	### Measurable Outcomes
132	
133	- **SC-001**: 100% of returning users with a valid stored session reach Home/Chat automatically after the splash state, with no login step required.
134	- **SC-002**: A new user can go from the sign-up form to a usable Home/Chat screen in a single successful attempt, with no intermediate screen other than the brief splash state.
135	- **SC-003**: Every error condition that sign-up, login, session-renewal, and session-check can return produces a readable on-screen message rather than a blank screen, a crash, or an indefinite loading state.
136	- **SC-004**: A user can reach each of the main screens (Home/Chat, Meus Registros, Configurações) from the side menu, and return to Home/Chat, in 2 taps or fewer, every time.
137	- **SC-005**: When a session expires while a screen is in a particular state, that same state (e.g., scroll position, visible content) is unchanged after the user re-authenticates, in every observed case.
138	- **SC-006**: Every screen delivered by this unit visually matches the prototype's documented colors, typography, and spacing, with zero visual values defined outside the single central source.
139	
140	## Assumptions
141	
142	- Biometric/PIN authentication (RF03) is its own delivery unit, built immediately after this one. Until it exists, the splash state routes directly between itself and the login/sign-up screen — the biometric step shown in the prototype's navigation map is intentionally skipped for this unit and will be inserted by the RF03 unit.
143	- Re-authenticating from the "Sessão expirada" overlay goes to the login screen (not to a biometric step), for the same reason — RF03 is not yet part of the app.
144	- Sign-up collects only an email and a password, matching both the prototype (which shows no additional fields) and the backend's sign-up contract.
145	- Session renewal is attempted silently in the background whenever a request fails because the session has merely expired; the "Sessão expirada" overlay is shown only once silent renewal itself is not possible.
146	- Where this unit's side menu is shown, "Planos de Ação" may exist as an inert placeholder entry per the product's extension-feature policy, but is not required navigation for this unit — only Home/Chat, Meus Registros, and Configurações are.
147	- Access and refresh tokens are kept on the device between app launches so a returning user is not asked to log in every time; the specific on-device storage mechanism is an implementation choice, not fixed by this specification.
148	- Every error this unit's calls (sign-up, login, refresh, session check) can return is one of the backend's fixed, documented error codes; no other error shape is expected from these calls.
149

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: 100% of returning users with a valid stored session reach Home/Chat automatically after the splash state, with no login step required.
- **SC-002**: A new user can go from the sign-up form to a usable Home/Chat screen in a single successful attempt, with no intermediate screen other than the brief splash state.
- **SC-003**: Every error condition that sign-up, login, session-renewal, and session-check can return produces a readable on-screen message rather than a blank screen, a crash, or an indefinite loading state.
- **SC-004**: A user can reach each of the main screens (Home/Chat, Meus Registros, Configurações) from the side menu, and return to Home/Chat, in 2 taps or fewer, every time.
- **SC-005**: When a session expires while a screen is in a particular state, that same state (e.g., scroll position, visible content) is unchanged after the user re-authenticates, in every observed case.
- **SC-006**: Every screen delivered by this unit visually matches the prototype's documented colors, typography, and spacing, with zero visual values defined outside the single central source.

## Assumptions

- Biometric/PIN authentication (RF03) is its own delivery unit, built immediately after this one. Until it exists, the splash state routes directly between itself and the login/sign-up screen — the biometric step shown in the prototype's navigation map is intentionally skipped for this unit and will be inserted by the RF03 unit.
- Re-authenticating from the "Sessão expirada" overlay goes to the login screen (not to a biometric step), for the same reason — RF03 is not yet part of the app.
- Sign-up collects only an email and a password, matching both the prototype (which shows no additional fields) and the backend's sign-up contract.
- Session renewal is attempted silently in the background whenever a request fails because the session has merely expired; the "Sessão expirada" overlay is shown only once silent renewal itself is not possible.
- Where this unit's side menu is shown, "Planos de Ação" may exist as an inert placeholder entry per the product's extension-feature policy, but is not required navigation for this unit — only Home/Chat, Meus Registros, and Configurações are.
- Access and refresh tokens are kept on the device between app launches so a returning user is not asked to log in every time; the specific on-device storage mechanism is an implementation choice, not fixed by this specification.
- Every error this unit's calls (sign-up, login, refresh, session check) can return is one of the backend's fixed, documented error codes; no other error shape is expected from these calls.

1	# Research: P-F000 — Foundation
2	
3	Every item below was a "NEEDS CLARIFICATION" or a constitution-flagged "free" choice (routing, HTTP
4	client, local cache, DI, secure storage, biometrics, charting). Biometrics and charting are not
5	exercised by F000, so they are left open for the units that need them (RF03, RF09).
6	
7	## R1 — Flutter/Dart version to pin via `fvm`
8	
9	- **Decision**: Pin this project to Flutter `3.47.5` / Dart `3.13.4`, stable channel.
10	- **Rationale**: The constitution fixes "Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`" but no
11	  `.fvmrc` exists yet in this repo — F000 is where the pin is created. `fvm list` on this machine
12	  already shows `3.47.5`/stable cached as the global default (released 2026-09-18), avoiding a
13	  fresh multi-GB download and giving a reproducible, already-verified SDK.
14	- **Alternatives considered**: Pinning an older LTS-style version — rejected, no such version is
15	  already available locally and the constitution expresses no preference for anything but
16	  "the version pinned via fvm," which this satisfies directly.
17	
18	## R2 — HTTP client
19	
20	- **Decision**: `dio`.
21	- **Rationale**: FR-003/FR-004 require one call surface that always yields `Either<Failure, T>`
22	  and uniformly translates `{code, message, retryable, requestId}` into a typed failure; Principle
23	  III requires injecting `apikey` and the right `Authorization` value per call. `dio`'s
24	  `Interceptor` API is the natural place to inject both headers once and to centralize
25	  timeout/malformed/offline detection for every later unit's write endpoints (RNF09), rather than
26	  repeating that logic per repository.
27	- **Alternatives considered**: `package:http` — would need a hand-rolled interceptor-equivalent
28	  layer for header injection and timeout classification, duplicating what `dio` gives for free;
29	  rejected as unnecessary extra surface for no benefit given `dio` is already the de-facto standard
30	  paired with `flutter_bloc` + `fpdart` repositories.
31	
32	## R3 — Routing and the two "overlay" requirements (side menu, Sessão expirada)
33	
34	- **Decision**: `go_router` for top-level screen navigation, with a single root `Navigator` stack
35	  (`context.push`, not `go`/`replace`, from the side menu). The side menu itself is a plain
36	  `Scaffold.drawer` (`Drawer` widget), not a route. The "Sessão expirada" overlay is a
37	  non-dismissible `showDialog` raised through a root `navigatorKey` whenever `SessionBloc` observes
38	  an `AUTH_EXPIRED` failure that silent refresh could not resolve.
39	- **Rationale**: FR-013/FR-014 and User Story 5 require the screen underneath the overlay to keep
40	  its exact state (e.g., scroll position). Flutter never disposes a `State` object that is merely
41	  covered by a drawer or by a dialog route pushed on top of it — only `push`ing (not `go`/replacing)
42	  guarantees this for screen-to-screen navigation too (FR-011, User Story 4: "returning to
43	  Home/Chat, confirming Home/Chat's state unchanged"). This reaches both behaviors without a
44	  nested/branch-navigation scheme.
45	- **Alternatives considered**: `StatefulShellRoute` (go_router's persistent-tab branches) — gives
46	  the same state-preservation guarantee but is built for bottom-nav-style parallel branches; Meus
47	  Registros/Configurações are occasional side-menu destinations, not a tab bar, so plain stack
48	  `push` is the simpler fit. A hand-built `Overlay`/`OverlayEntry` for the expired-session case was
49	  considered instead of `showDialog` — rejected: `showDialog` already is an overlay route with a
50	  scrim, matching the prototype's "centered card over a light scrim" description with less custom
51	  code.
52	
53	## R4 — Dependency injection / service location
54	
55	- **Decision**: `get_it`, with manual registration (no code generation).
56	- **Rationale**: F000 only wires a handful of singletons (`ApiClient`, `SecureTokenStorage`, two
57	  repositories, two blocs-as-factories). `get_it` is the standard pairing with `flutter_bloc` for
58	  exposing repositories/use cases to `BlocProvider`s without threading them through constructors
59	  manually, and manual registration avoids adding a build-time code-gen dependency for a graph this
60	  small.
61	- **Alternatives considered**: `injectable` (codegen over `get_it`) — rejected for now as
62	  premature; the registration list is small enough that generated code would add build complexity
63	  without a proportional benefit. Can be introduced later without touching domain code if the
64	  graph grows.
65	
66	## R5 — On-device secure storage for tokens
67	
68	- **Decision**: `flutter_secure_storage`.
69	- **Rationale**: Assumptions in spec.md require access/refresh tokens to survive app restarts; the
70	  app ships iOS-only, where `flutter_secure_storage` backs onto the Keychain — appropriate for
71	  credentials, unlike unencrypted `shared_preferences`.
72	- **Alternatives considered**: `shared_preferences` — rejected, stores in plaintext and is
73	  unsuitable for refresh tokens even on a single-platform (iOS) app.
74	
75	## R6 — Error/Failure mapping scope
76	
77	- **Decision**: `core/network/failure.dart` models all 13 closed error codes from
78	  `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` now, even though F000's own 4 endpoints can only return a
79	  subset of them.
80	- **Rationale**: FR-004 says the system must translate "every backend error response['s] error
81	  code" — worded generically, not scoped to F000's own calls — and this file is exactly the shared
82	  piece "no single requirement owns but all of them use" that requirements.md §12 assigns to F000.
83	  Defining it once now means RF01–RF09 never need to touch this file, only add usages of it.
84	- **Alternatives considered**: Mapping only the codes F000's endpoints can return (`AUTH_EXPIRED`,
85	  `AUTH_INVALID`, `NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, `NETWORK_OFFLINE`, `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `RATE_LIMITED`) and
86	  letting later units extend the hierarchy — rejected: the taxonomy is explicitly closed and fully
87	  known today, so extending it later would be a pure mechanical addition with no new information,
88	  while leaving it incomplete risks a later unit quietly handling an "unknown" code path instead of
89	  its real typed `Failure`.
90	
91	## R7 — Splash-time session check under a network failure
92	
93	- **Decision**: If `GET auth-session` (or the subsequent `POST auth-refresh` fallback) itself fails
94	  with `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` or `NETWORK_OFFLINE` — as opposed to resolving to `AUTH_EXPIRED`/

# Research: P-F000 — Foundation

Every item below was a "NEEDS CLARIFICATION" or a constitution-flagged "free" choice (routing, HTTP
client, local cache, DI, secure storage, biometrics, charting). Biometrics and charting are not
exercised by F000, so they are left open for the units that need them (RF03, RF09).

## R1 — Flutter/Dart version to pin via `fvm`

- **Decision**: Pin this project to Flutter `3.47.5` / Dart `3.13.4`, stable channel.
- **Rationale**: The constitution fixes "Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`" but no
  `.fvmrc` exists yet in this repo — F000 is where the pin is created. `fvm list` on this machine
  already shows `3.47.5`/stable cached as the global default (released 2026-09-18), avoiding a
  fresh multi-GB download and giving a reproducible, already-verified SDK.
- **Alternatives considered**: Pinning an older LTS-style version — rejected, no such version is
  already available locally and the constitution expresses no preference for anything but
  "the version pinned via fvm," which this satisfies directly.

## R2 — HTTP client

- **Decision**: `dio`.
- **Rationale**: FR-003/FR-004 require one call surface that always yields `Either<Failure, T>`
  and uniformly translates `{code, message, retryable, requestId}` into a typed failure; Principle
  III requires injecting `apikey` and the right `Authorization` value per call. `dio`'s
  `Interceptor` API is the natural place to inject both headers once and to centralize
  timeout/malformed/offline detection for every later unit's write endpoints (RNF09), rather than
  repeating that logic per repository.
- **Alternatives considered**: `package:http` — would need a hand-rolled interceptor-equivalent
  layer for header injection and timeout classification, duplicating what `dio` gives for free;
  rejected as unnecessary extra surface for no benefit given `dio` is already the de-facto standard
  paired with `flutter_bloc` + `fpdart` repositories.

## R3 — Routing and the two "overlay" requirements (side menu, Sessão expirada)

- **Decision**: `go_router` for top-level screen navigation, with a single root `Navigator` stack
  (`context.push`, not `go`/`replace`, from the side menu). The side menu itself is a plain
  `Scaffold.drawer` (`Drawer` widget), not a route. The "Sessão expirada" overlay is a
  non-dismissible `showDialog` raised through a root `navigatorKey` whenever `SessionBloc` observes
  an `AUTH_EXPIRED` failure that silent refresh could not resolve.
- **Rationale**: FR-013/FR-014 and User Story 5 require the screen underneath the overlay to keep
  its exact state (e.g., scroll position). Flutter never disposes a `State` object that is merely
  covered by a drawer or by a dialog route pushed on top of it — only `push`ing (not `go`/replacing)
  guarantees this for screen-to-screen navigation too (FR-011, User Story 4: "returning to
  Home/Chat, confirming Home/Chat's state unchanged"). This reaches both behaviors without a
  nested/branch-navigation scheme.
- **Alternatives considered**: `StatefulShellRoute` (go_router's persistent-tab branches) — gives
  the same state-preservation guarantee but is built for bottom-nav-style parallel branches; Meus
  Registros/Configurações are occasional side-menu destinations, not a tab bar, so plain stack
  `push` is the simpler fit. A hand-built `Overlay`/`OverlayEntry` for the expired-session case was
  considered instead of `showDialog` — rejected: `showDialog` already is an overlay route with a
  scrim, matching the prototype's "centered card over a light scrim" description with less custom
  code.

## R4 — Dependency injection / service location

- **Decision**: `get_it`, with manual registration (no code generation).
- **Rationale**: F000 only wires a handful of singletons (`ApiClient`, `SecureTokenStorage`, two
  repositories, two blocs-as-factories). `get_it` is the standard pairing with `flutter_bloc` for
  exposing repositories/use cases to `BlocProvider`s without threading them through constructors
  manually, and manual registration avoids adding a build-time code-gen dependency for a graph this
  small.
- **Alternatives considered**: `injectable` (codegen over `get_it`) — rejected for now as
  premature; the registration list is small enough that generated code would add build complexity
  without a proportional benefit. Can be introduced later without touching domain code if the
  graph grows.

## R5 — On-device secure storage for tokens

- **Decision**: `flutter_secure_storage`.
- **Rationale**: Assumptions in spec.md require access/refresh tokens to survive app restarts; the
  app ships iOS-only, where `flutter_secure_storage` backs onto the Keychain — appropriate for
  credentials, unlike unencrypted `shared_preferences`.
- **Alternatives considered**: `shared_preferences` — rejected, stores in plaintext and is
  unsuitable for refresh tokens even on a single-platform (iOS) app.

## R6 — Error/Failure mapping scope

- **Decision**: `core/network/failure.dart` models all 13 closed error codes from
  `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` now, even though F000's own 4 endpoints can only return a
  subset of them.
- **Rationale**: FR-004 says the system must translate "every backend error response['s] error
  code" — worded generically, not scoped to F000's own calls — and this file is exactly the shared
  piece "no single requirement owns but all of them use" that requirements.md §12 assigns to F000.
  Defining it once now means RF01–RF09 never need to touch this file, only add usages of it.
- **Alternatives considered**: Mapping only the codes F000's endpoints can return (`AUTH_EXPIRED`,
  `AUTH_INVALID`, `NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, `NETWORK_OFFLINE`, `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `RATE_LIMITED`) and
  letting later units extend the hierarchy — rejected: the taxonomy is explicitly closed and fully
  known today, so extending it later would be a pure mechanical addition with no new information,
  while leaving it incomplete risks a later unit quietly handling an "unknown" code path instead of
  its real typed `Failure`.

## R7 — Splash-time session check under a network failure

  user who does have a valid stored session but is momentarily offline; silently retrying forever
  would leave them stuck. A visible retry affordance satisfies "never stuck" without discarding a
  potentially-valid session. This is the reasonable technical decision Constitution Principle I
  calls for where the inputs are silent.
- **Alternatives considered**: Auto-retry with exponential backoff and no user action — rejected,
  can still leave the user staring at the splash indefinitely on sustained offline, which the spec's
  edge cases explicitly want to avoid.

## R8 — iOS minimum deployment target

- **Decision**: Leave it at whatever `flutter create` generates for the pinned 3.47.5 SDK; do not
  override it.
- **Rationale**: Neither requirements.md nor the constitution states a minimum iOS version — only
  "iOS, portrait only." Inventing a specific floor (e.g., "iOS 15+") would be an unrequested,
  unverifiable constraint. The SDK's own default is the reasonable technical decision here per
  Constitution Principle I.
- **Alternatives considered**: None — there is no documented requirement to weigh against.

## R9 — `design_tokens.dart` shape and font delivery

- **Decision**: A plain Dart class of `static const` values (colors as `Color`, type scale as
  `TextStyle`, spacing/radii as `double`) feeding a single `ThemeData` built from those constants;
  fonts (`Fraunces`, `Karla`, `IBM Plex Mono`) are bundled as local assets declared in
  `pubspec.yaml`, not fetched at runtime.
- **Rationale**: RNF08 requires zero hardcoded visual values outside this one file — a `static
  const` class makes any other hardcoded value a compile-time-visible outlier (not referencing the
  token file) rather than something only caught by review. Bundling fonts as assets (vs.
  `google_fonts`, which fetches over the network on first use) avoids adding a second runtime
  network dependency beyond the backend itself and keeps text rendering deterministic offline,
  consistent with RNF01's latency intent.
- **Alternatives considered**: `google_fonts` package — rejected: introduces a non-backend network
  fetch and a cache-miss failure mode (slow/no connection on first launch) that bundled assets don't
  have. Obtaining and vendoring the three actual font files is left as an implementation task
  (tasks.md), since this plan does not fetch external binary assets.

## R10 — Home/Chat shell scope under FR-016

- **Decision**: The Home/Chat screen F000 ships shows the fixed header (☰ + "Cerne" wordmark per
  the prototype) and an empty conversation area, plus a composer bar that is rendered but fully
  **disabled** (text field non-editable, send button non-interactive) — no fake messages, no RF04
  wiring.
- **Rationale**: FR-016 allows RF01–RF10 controls to "exist only as an inert placeholder, if at

- **Alternatives considered**: Omitting the composer entirely and showing only an empty state —

end. Interface details (headers, URLs, failure types) are in `contracts/`; entity/state details

## Prerequisites

## Setup

## Automated checks

```bash
fvm flutter analyze                                   # 0 issues, incl. no flutter imports under domain/ (RNF06)
fvm flutter test --coverage                            # unit + bloc tests (mocktail, bloc_test)
lcov --extract coverage/lcov.info 'lib/*/domain/*' -o coverage/domain.info
genhtml coverage/domain.info -o coverage/domain_html    # inspect: >= 80% (RNF07)
```

## Manual / integration validation scenarios

Each maps directly to a spec.md Acceptance Scenario.

1. **Login (User Story 1)**
   - Launch with no stored session → login screen.
   - Enter a valid, existing email/password → lands on Home/Chat.
   - Enter a wrong password → inline, non-crashing error, stays on login screen, can retry.
   - Turn off network, submit → retryable connection-error message, no hang/crash.

2. **Sign-up (User Story 2)**
   - From the login screen, tap the toggle link → title/CTA switch to "Criar conta" (same screen,
     no navigation).
   - Submit a brand-new email/password → account created, lands directly on Home/Chat.
   - Submit an already-registered email → clear error, form stays editable, no crash.

3. **Launch routing (User Story 3)** — exercise all three stored-session conditions:
   - Valid session on device → splash, then straight to Home/Chat, no credentials re-entered.
   - No stored session (fresh install, or after a manual token wipe) → splash, then login screen.
   - Expired-but-refreshable session (manually expire the stored `accessToken`, keep a valid
     `refreshToken`) → splash, silent `auth-refresh`, lands on Home/Chat without any prompt.

4. **Base navigation (User Story 4)**
   - From Home/Chat, open the drawer (☰) → see Meus Registros, Configurações.
   - Visit Meus Registros, return to Home/Chat → chat shell state (e.g., scroll position) unchanged.
   - Same for Configurações.
   - Opening the drawer itself visibly scrims the current screen without resetting it.

5. **Session-expired overlay (User Story 5)**
   - Get to a known state on a screen (e.g., scroll Home/Chat partway).
   - Force a session-expired response (e.g., revoke/expire the access token server-side, or stub it
     in a debug build) while that screen is active.
   - Confirm the "Sessão expirada" card appears over a light scrim, screen content still visible
     and unchanged underneath.
   - Tap "Entrar novamente", re-authenticate → overlay dismissed, screen state (scroll position)
     restored exactly.
   - Repeat the forced expiry while the overlay is still visible (before dismissing) → overlay
     persists/reappears rather than letting the user proceed.

## Expected outcome

All 5 scenarios above pass; `flutter analyze` and `flutter test --coverage` are clean; the
`lib/**/domain/**` coverage report meets RNF07; no screen's rendered output uses a color, font, or
spacing value traceable to anything other than `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (spot-check via code
review, since this is not yet an automated lint in this unit).

# Contract: `ApiClient` (`lib/core/network/api_client.dart`)

The single way any feature calls the backend (FR-003). Every later unit's `data/` layer depends on
this, never on `dio` directly.

## Construction

```dart
class ApiClient {
  ApiClient({required Dio dio, required SecureTokenStorage tokenStorage, required String anonKey});

  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> call(
    String function, {               // e.g. "auth-login" — never a REST path (FR-005)
    required String method,          // "GET" | "POST" | "PATCH" | "DELETE"
    Map<String, dynamic>? body,
    List<String>? pathSegments,      // appended in the order the OpenAPI path declares them
    AuthMode authMode = AuthMode.userSession, // or AuthMode.anonKey
  });
}

enum AuthMode { anonKey, userSession }
```

## Behavior

1. **URL construction**: `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>/<pathSegments...>` — read from `.env`'s
   `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`. Never the OpenAPI document's REST-notation path (Principle III, FR-005).
2. **Headers, every call**: `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>` (from `.env`).
3. **`Authorization` header**:
   - `AuthMode.anonKey` → `Bearer <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>` — used for `auth-signup`, `auth-login`,
     `auth-refresh` (no user session exists yet or is being replaced).
   - `AuthMode.userSession` → `Bearer <stored accessToken>` (read from `SecureTokenStorage`) — used
     for `auth-session` and every `bearerAuth` operation added by later units.
4. **Success**: returns `Right(data)` where `data` is the parsed `data` object from the response
   envelope (`{data, meta}`), discarding `meta` unless a future unit's contract says otherwise.
5. **Failure**: any non-2xx response with the `{code, message, retryable, requestId}` error body is
   passed to `ErrorMapper.fromResponse(...)` → `Left(Failure)` (see `failure-taxonomy.md`). A dio
   `DioExceptionType.connectionError`/no-response condition is mapped directly to
   `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure(...))` without a parse attempt (error-taxonomy.md: `NETWORK_OFFLINE`
   never arrives as an HTTP response). A dio timeout is mapped to `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure(...))`.
6. **Never throws** past this boundary — every exception dio can raise is caught and mapped to a
   `Failure` before returning, satisfying FR-003 ("never an unhandled crash").

## Who depends on this

`AuthRemoteDataSource`, `SessionRemoteDataSource` (this unit) and every later unit's `*RemoteDataSource`.

1	# Contract: `SessionRepository` (`lib/features/session/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart`)
2	
3	Domain-layer interface owning the session lifecycle: launch-time check, silent refresh, and
4	reading/clearing the stored session. `SessionBloc` depends on this and on nothing in
5	`session/data/` or `auth/data/` directly (RNF06).
6	
7	```dart
8	abstract class SessionRepository {
9	  Future<Either<Failure, Session>> checkSession();     // GET auth-session, using the stored accessToken
10	  Future<Either<Failure, Session>> refresh();           // POST auth-refresh, using the stored refreshToken
11	  Future<void> persist(Session session);                 // write-through to SecureTokenStorage
12	  Future<void> clear();                                   // logout / failed-refresh cleanup
13	  Future<bool> hasStoredSession();                        // true iff a refreshToken is present on device
14	}
15	```
16	
17	- **`checkSession`** → FR-009's first step. `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)` is the expected, non-error
18	  trigger for the caller (`CheckSessionUseCase`) to then call `refresh()` — not itself a terminal
19	  failure shown to the user.
20	- **`refresh`** → FR-009's renewal step, also reused for the silent-refresh-before-overlay path of
21	  FR-013 (User Story 5) and for any later unit's authenticated call that comes back
22	  `AUTH_EXPIRED`. On `Right`, calls `persist()` internally before returning.
23	- **`persist`/`clear`** → thin wrappers over `SecureTokenStorage`; exposed on the repository (not
24	  the data source) so the domain layer's use cases never import `storage/` directly.
25	- **`hasStoredSession`** → lets `CheckSessionUseCase` skip the network call entirely when there is
26	  nothing to check (Edge Cases / User Story 3 scenario 2: no stored session → straight to login,
27	  no call made).
28	
29	## `CheckSessionUseCase` (orchestration, domain layer)
30	
31	```dart
32	Future<SessionStatus> call() async {
33	  if (!await repo.hasStoredSession()) return SessionStatus.unauthenticated;
34	  final checked = await repo.checkSession();
35	  return checked.match(
36	    (failure) => failure is AuthExpiredFailure
37	        ? _tryRefresh()
38	        : SessionStatus.networkError(failure),      // R7 — splash retry affordance, not a route change
39	    (session) => SessionStatus.authenticated(session),
40	  );
41	}
42	
43	Future<SessionStatus> _tryRefresh() async {
44	  final refreshed = await repo.refresh();
45	  return refreshed.match(
46	    (failure) async { await repo.clear(); return SessionStatus.unauthenticated; },
47	    (session) => SessionStatus.authenticated(session),
48	  );
49	}
50	```
51	
52	This single use case is what `SplashPage`/`SessionBloc` calls — it is the only place FR-009's
53	"renew first, then route" rule is implemented, so later units never re-derive it.
54	
55	## Who depends on this
56	
57	`SessionBloc` (splash routing, FR-010; expired-session overlay trigger, FR-013/FR-014). Every later
58	unit that makes an authenticated call and receives `AuthExpiredFailure` calls `SessionRepository
59	.refresh()` the same way, through this interface — never by re-implementing the refresh call.
60

# Cerne Constitution

## Core Principles

### I. Product Source of Truth
`docs/input/` — `requirements.md`, `prototype/`, and `backend/` — is the
authoritative source for product behavior. `requirements.md` defines
functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery
order, and technical constraints; `prototype/` is the frozen visual
reference and its token/state extract; `backend/` documents the existing
API, error taxonomy, screen-state map, sync-badge semantics, and fixtures.
Where these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable
technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under
`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
this repository.

Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
stable.

### II. Fixed Technology Stack
The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
and charting — are open implementation decisions.

Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
built by different contributors or at different times.

### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
NEVER be committed.

Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
credential leakage.

### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
documentation MUST be in English.

Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
preserving the product's voice.

### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
Code MUST follow the folder convention:
```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```
The domain layer MUST comply with RNF06: zero layer violations — it MUST
NOT import `package:flutter` nor any class from a feature's `data/` layer.

Rationale: a fixed, enforced folder shape and a flutter/data-free domain
layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules
portable regardless of UI or persistence choices.

## Quality Standards (RNF01–RNF09)

These targets from `docs/input/requirements.md` are binding quality gates:

- **RNF01 — Interaction latency**: a local action MUST be reflected in the
  UI in under 100 ms; any network call taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a
  loading indicator.
- **RNF02 — PII stripping**: performed backend-side via Claude Haiku 4.5
  with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model; the app
  implements no PII-detection logic of its own.
- **RNF03 — Zero data retention**: a backend-side policy; the app MUST NOT
  introduce its own retention beyond what the backend requires.
- **RNF04 — Row Level Security (RLS)**: enforced backend-side; the app MUST
  assume RLS is authoritative and MUST NEVER attempt to bypass it.
- **RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD)**: the app MUST expose
  the account-deletion flow (`DELETE /account`) from Settings.
- **RNF06 — Zero layer violations**: see Principle V; 0 violations is the
  target.
- **RNF07 — Domain test coverage**: `lib/**/domain/**` MUST reach at least
  80% test coverage.
- **RNF08 — Visual fidelity**: every screen MUST match the prototype's
  color, typography, and spacing, with 0 hardcoded visual values outside
  `design_tokens.dart`.
- **RNF09 — Consistent network-error handling**: every repository MUST use
  the `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart`; every write endpoint (5

  failures, each covered by `mocktail` tests (15 of 15 scenarios).

  `docs/input/requirements.md`.
- Extension features (section 2 of `requirements.md`) are explicitly out of
  scope and MUST NOT be implemented beyond an optional placeholder menu
  entry.
- The following actions are prohibited in this repository:
  - Changing the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
  - Calling AI providers directly from the app.
  - Writing visual values (colors, font sizes, spacing, radii) outside
    `design_tokens.dart`.
  - Implementing extension features.
  - Committing `.env` or any credential.
  - Editing files under `docs/input/`.

## Governance

This constitution supersedes any conflicting practice, template, or
instruction used in this repository. Every plan, spec, task list, and
review MUST verify compliance with these principles before work is
considered done; any deviation MUST be justified in writing in the relevant
artifact (plan or PR description) or the work MUST be rejected.

**Amendment procedure**: amendments are proposed by editing this file,
describing the change and rationale, and are adopted once the project owner
accepts the change (commit to this file constitutes adoption in this
single-maintainer project). Each amendment MUST update the Sync Impact
Report at the top of this file and the version/date line below.

**Versioning policy** (semantic versioning for this document):
- **MAJOR** — backward-incompatible governance or principle removal/
  redefinition.
- **MINOR** — a new principle or section added, or materially expanded
  guidance.
- **PATCH** — wording clarifications, typo fixes, non-semantic refinements.

**Compliance review**: any change to `lib/` MUST be checked against the
Core Principles and Quality Standards above before merge; violations of
RNF06–RNF09 in particular are release blockers.

openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Cerne Backend API
  description: '**How to build the real URL:** there is no router — each operation is served by its own Edge Function,
    one per endpoint. The `path` of each operation below is only the contract''s REST notation; the real URL is
    `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path parameters, in the same order as they appear in the `path`, as
    final segments>` — any literal segment of the `path` after the last parameter (e.g., the `/retry` of `/chat/sessions/{id}/messages/{userMessageId}/retry`)
    does NOT appear in the real URL. Each operation carries the function name in `x-cerne-function`; the full path
    → function table is in `docs/input/backend/README.md`.'
  version: 1.0.0
servers:
- url: '{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}'
  variables:
    FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL:
      default: https://<project-ref>.functions.supabase.co
      description: Base URL of the environment's Edge Functions — the `project ref` of the environment is provided
        in the app's `.env`, never in this file.
paths:
  /auth/signup:
    post:
      operationId: auth.signup
      summary: Sign-up — thin GoTrue proxy
      security: []
      x-cerne-function: auth-signup
      requestBody:
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Error'
  /auth/login:
    post:
      operationId: auth.login
      summary: Login — thin GoTrue proxy
      security: []
      x-cerne-function: auth-login
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Error'
  /auth/refresh:
    post:
      operationId: auth.refresh
      summary: Token refresh — thin GoTrue proxy
      security: []
      x-cerne-function: auth-refresh
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
        default:
          description: Error
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Error'
  /auth/session:
    get:
      operationId: auth.session
      summary: Current session — the only auth endpoint with its own logic
      security:
      - bearerAuth: []
      x-cerne-function: auth-session
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Success

content.content:
# Cerne — Prototype extract

The visual reference of the product is `cerne-prototype.html` (this folder). Open it in a browser; it needs JavaScript. This extract lists its navigable states, its visual tokens, its components and the implementation notes that come with it.

- **Frame:** 390 × 844 logical points, portrait only, 4 dp grid.
- **Language of the interface:** Portuguese. Every UI text below appears exactly as in the prototype, in quotes.
- **Precedence:** the prototype defines appearance and states. Behavior rules (triggers, timings, filters, error handling) are defined in `docs/input/requirements.md`; where the prototype's simulated behavior differs from a requirement, the requirement prevails.

---

## 1. Navigation map

The prototype has **32 navigable states**, reachable from a single state machine (a `screen` variable plus overlay flags). Not every state is a new full screen — several are **overlays** (modal, sheet, bottom sheet, dialog) shown on top of one of three base screens: **Home/Chat**, **Meus Registros** and **Configurações**. Overlays preserve the screen underneath (it stays visible, with a darkened scrim behind).

```
Splash (auto, 1.8 s)
  └─> Biometria ──tap/error──> PIN inicial / PIN após falha
  │      └─> "usar e-mail e senha" ──> Entrar / criar conta (toggle)
  │                                          └─> submit ──> Home/Chat
  └─(PIN complete, 4 digits)──> Home/Chat
  └─(Face ID/Touch ID ok)──> Home/Chat

Home/Chat (base screen)
  ├─ overlay: Sessão expirada (backend session expires; "Entrar novamente" ──> Biometria)
  ├─ overlay: side menu (☰ icon) ──> Meus Registros | Planos de Ação | Configurações | new conversation
  └─ overlay: Insertion modal ("+" button) ──> tabs Texto / Áudio / Foto, each with its own sub-states
        (on save, the modal closes and returns to Home/Chat with the record added)

Meus Registros (base screen, from the side menu)
  ├─ empty state (no records) ──CTA "Criar primeiro registro"──> Insertion modal
  ├─ overlay: filter sheet ──"Aplicar"──> active filters (chips on the list)
  └─ overlay: export card (download icon) ──> pending ──> processing ──> done | error | empty period

Planos de Ação (base screen, from the side menu) — static screen, 3-column kanban (extension, not implemented)

Configurações (base screen, from the side menu)
  ├─ dashboard variations: zero entries | one entry | more than 30 (with narrative) | narrative unavailable
  ├─ inline profile-name editing
  ├─ AI persona selection (Analítico / Empático / Socrático) (extension, not implemented)
  ├─ "Sair" ──> Biometria
  └─ overlay: account-deletion confirmation ──"Apagar tudo"──> Biometria (same destination as logout)
```

---

## 2. Navigable states

Names as they appear in the prototype. The prototype's own state catalog has 32 entries: Tela 0 — Splash; Tela 0.1 — Biometria; Tela 0.1a — Entrar / criar conta; Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial; Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha; Tela 1 — Home / Chat; Tela 2 — Texto, Áudio (Gravando, Processando, Transcrito, Erro), Foto (Captura, Processando OCR, Reconhecido, Erro); Tela 3 — Menu lateral; Tela 1 — Sessão expirada; Tela 4 — Meus Registros, Estado vazio, Sheet de filtro, Filtros ativos; Exportar — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio; Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]**; Tela 6 — Configurações, Dashboard zero entradas, Dashboard uma entrada, Narrativa indisponível, Confirmar exclusão. The tables below group them by screen; some rows describe variations inside one state (e.g., the bookmark sub-states, the streaming response). Extension states (requirements, section 2) are marked **[ext]**.

### 2.1 Entry and authentication
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 0 — Splash | Wordmark "Cerne" centered on dark green, 3 loading dots; lasts 1.8 s and moves on automatically. |
| Tela 0.1 — Biometria | Fingerprint circle, title "Toque para desbloquear", link "Usar PIN", secondary link "usar e-mail e senha" near the bottom. |
| Tela 0.1a — Entrar | Login mode: title "Bem-vindo de volta", fields E-mail and Senha, CTA "Entrar", toggle link, link "usar biometria". |
| Tela 0.1a — Criar conta | Same screen in sign-up mode: title "Crie sua conta", CTA "Criar conta" (toggled by a text link, not a separate screen). |
| Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial | Title "Digite seu PIN", 4 progress dots, 3×4 numeric keypad with backspace; after the 4th digit, moves on after 350 ms. |
| Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha | Same as 0.1b plus the error band "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN". |

### 2.2 Conversation
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 1 — Home/Chat (default) | Messages going back and forth; dark green fixed header with ☰ and wordmark; composer with "+", placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...", send icon. |
| Tela 1 — Streaming | AI response revealed progressively with a pulsing cursor. |
| Tela 1 — Insight | Insight card with ochre spine, label "INSIGHT", "x" to dismiss, interleaved in the messages. |
| Tela 1 — Falha ao gerar resposta | Incomplete AI message with "Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente" in red, in place of the time. |
| Tela 1 — Bookmark | Bookmark on each user message with 4 sub-states: `idle`, `saving` (spinner), `saved` (ochre check), `error` (red warning). |
| Tela 1 — Offline | Blue-gray banner "Sem conexão — histórico disponível, novas mensagens bloqueadas"; send icon disabled. |
| Tela 1 — Sessão expirada | Light scrim over the chat (still readable), centered card with lock icon, title "Sessão expirada", text saying history and scroll position are kept, button "Entrar novamente". |
| Tela 3 — Menu lateral | Drawer: initials avatar and name; section "CONVERSAS" with past sessions (title + timestamp); items "Meus Registros", "Planos de Ação", "Configurações"; new-conversation action. |

### 2.3 Insertion modal (bottom sheet over Home/Chat; 9 states)
Common structure: "x" to close and a 3-tab bar (Texto / Áudio / Foto); the active tab has a filled dark-green background.

| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Texto | Multiline field, placeholder "Escreva livremente...", button "Salvar". |
| Áudio — Gravando | Red stop button, animated 12-bar waveform, monospace timer (e.g., "00:12"). |
| Áudio — Processando | Spinner in place of stop; frozen, faded waveform (opacity .35); text "Transcrevendo..."; label "00:42 de áudio". |
| Áudio — Transcrito | Editable transcribed text; original audio duration in mono; "Salvar" enabled. |
| Áudio — Erro | Red warning icon, "Não foi possível transcrever", outline button "Tentar novamente". |
| Foto — Captura | Two large buttons, "Câmera" and "Galeria". |
| Foto — Processando OCR | Photo thumbnail, spinner, "Reconhecendo texto...". |
| Foto — Reconhecido | Small thumbnail next to the extracted (editable) text; "Salvar". |
| Foto — Erro | Thumbnail kept, warning icon, "Não foi possível reconhecer o texto", button "Tentar novamente" and secondary text action "Salvar só a foto". |

### 2.4 Records
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 4 — Meus Registros (default) | Records grouped by date ("Hoje", "Ontem", dates); each card with a spine colored by origin, source icon, time, sync indicator (green "sincronizado" / ochre "sincronizando" / red "erro de sync"), text excerpt, category chips when present; header with back arrow, title, download icon; search bar "Buscar nos registros..." with a funnel button. |
| Tela 4 — Vazio | Large notebook icon, "Nenhum registro ainda", CTA "Criar primeiro registro". |
| Tela 4 — Filtros ativos | Removable chips under the search bar with the applied filters, link "Limpar filtros"; funnel button filled. |
| Tela 4 — Sheet de filtro | Groups "INTERVALO DE DATA" (Todo o período / Esta semana / Este mês, single choice), "CATEGORIA" (chips: trabalho, rotina, descanso, relações), "TIPO DE ENTRADA" (chips: manual, áudio, foto, chat); "Aplicar" and "Limpar". **Note:** the backend has no category filter (requirements, RF06); categories are the tags extension. |

### 2.5 Export (bottom sheet over Tela 4; 5 states)
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Pendente | Spinner, "Preparando exportação...". |
| Processando | "Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar. |
| Concluído | Green check, "Resumo pronto", buttons "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline). |
| Erro | Red warning; text explaining that the AI narrative failed but the data remains available; only the button "Baixar dados brutos". |
| Período vazio | "Nenhum registro nesse período." and a suggestion to adjust the filter; no download button. |

All five have the link "Fechar" at the bottom. The mapping between these states and the backend job statuses is in `docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`.

### 2.6 Plans and settings
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]** | Three horizontally scrolling columns — "A Fazer", "Em Andamento", "Concluído" — with counts and cards. |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — mais de 30 registros | "Sua evolução": 10-bar ochre chart + summary paragraph. |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — uma entrada | A single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias." |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — zero entradas | Light-gray chart icon in place of the chart and "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui"; no summary paragraph. |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — narrativa indisponível | Chart with data, but the AI summary paragraph failed — needs its own error message, not just missing text. |
| Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta | Centered dialog, red title "Apagar sua conta?", text on permanent, irreversible deletion; red button "Apagar tudo"; outline "Cancelar". |

Other elements of Configurações: avatar with editable name/e-mail (pencil becomes a check in edit mode — inline editing); persona cards "Como a IA responde" (Analítico, Empático, Socrático) **[ext]**; actions "Sair" and "Apagar conta" (red).

---

## 3. Visual system (tokens for `design_tokens.dart`)

The prototype has a **Design Tokens** panel, marked as the ground truth for `design_tokens.dart`. Its names and values are below.

### Colors
| Token | Hex | Use (as stated in the panel) |
|---|---|---|
| `colorPrimary` | `#1F3D34` | Buttons, app bar, wordmark |
| `colorPrimaryPressed` | `#16281F` | Pressed state |
| `colorOnPrimary` | `#F5F1E8` | Text on primary |
| `colorAccent` | `#C98A3E` | CTA, insight, saved bookmark |
| `colorOnAccent` | `#241C0D` | Text on accent |
| `colorSecondary` | `#7C8B6F` | Tags, chips, synchronizing |
| `colorSurfaceBg` | `#F2EFE7` | General background ("paper") |
| `colorSurfaceElevated` | `#FBF9F4` | Cards, bubbles, sheets |
| `colorBorder` | `#E1DACB` | Dividers, borders |
| `colorTextPrimary` | `#241F19` | Main text |
| `colorTextSecondary` | `#6B6255` | Secondary text |
| `colorError` | `#B3402A` | Errors, destructive action |
| `colorSuccess` | `#4C6B4F` | Synchronized, confirmations |
| `colorWarningSync` | `#C98A3E` | "Synchronizing" badge |
| `colorInfoOffline` | `#5C7A93` | Offline banner — single use |

Other colors that appear on specific screens but not in the panel: user chat bubble `#D9DFD3`; text on category chips `#3F4A38`.

### Typography
| Token | Font · weight · size/line-height | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `textDisplayLg` | Fraunces 600 · 32/38 | Splash wordmark |
| `textHeadlineMd` | Fraunces 600 · 24/30 | Section titles |
| `textTitleLg` | Karla 700 · 20/26 | App bar title |
| `textTitleSm` | Karla 700 · 16/22 | Subtitles |
| `textBodyLg` | Karla 400 · 16/24 | Bubbles, entries |
| `textBodyMd` | Karla 400 · 14/20 | Secondary text and descriptions |
| `textLabelMd` | Karla 500 · 13/18 | Button text, chips |
| `textMonoCaption` | IBM Plex Mono 500 · 12/16 · letter-spacing .2 | Technical metadata (timestamps, counters, status labels) |

### Spacing (4 dp grid)
`spacingXs` 4 · `spacingSm` 8 · `spacingMd` 16 · `spacingLg` 24 · `spacingXl` 32 · `spacing2xl` 48 (dp).

### Radii
`radiusSm` 8 dp (inputs, chips) · `radiusMd` 16 dp (cards, bubbles) · `radiusLg` 24 dp (sheets, modals) · `radiusFull` 999 dp (avatars, pills).

### Elevation
`elevation1` — `0 1px 3px rgba(36,31,25,.08)` (cards at rest) · `elevation2` — `0 4px 16px rgba(36,31,25,.14)` (sheets, modals).

### Icons

## 4. Special states that need extra care

- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.

2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.

## 1. Navigation map

The prototype has **32 navigable states**, reachable from a single state machine (a `screen` variable plus overlay flags). Not every state is a new full screen — several are **overlays** (modal, sheet, bottom sheet, dialog) shown on top of one of three base screens: **Home/Chat**, **Meus Registros** and **Configurações**. Overlays preserve the screen underneath (it stays visible, with a darkened scrim behind).

```

  │      └─> "usar e-mail e senha" ──> Entrar / criar conta (toggle)

# Tasks: P-F000 — Foundation

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/001-foundation/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/ (http-client.md,
failure-taxonomy.md, auth-repository.md, session-repository.md), quickstart.md — all present.

**Tests**: Included. `plan.md`'s Constitution Check marks RNF07 (domain coverage ≥80%) as
"PASS (gate carried into tasks)" and RNF09 requires 15/15 write-endpoint failure scenarios covered
by `mocktail`; `quickstart.md`'s Automated checks run `flutter test --coverage` against a
`lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter. Domain-layer unit tests (`mocktail`) and bloc tests (`bloc_test`)
are therefore generated per story; User Story 4 (pure navigation/presentation, no domain code) has
none, matching the domain-only scope of the gate.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (P1–P5 from spec.md) to enable independent

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies — start immediately.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup — BLOCKS all user stories.
- **User Stories (Phase 3–7)**: All depend on Foundational completion.
  - US1 (P1) has no dependency on another story.
  - US2 (P2) extends US1's `auth_remote_data_source.dart`/`auth_repository_impl.dart`/`auth_bloc.dart`/
    `login_signup_page.dart` in place — do US1 first.
  - US3 (P3) is independent of US1/US2's files but its splash routes to the Home/Chat page US1
    creates (T028) — do US1 first for a meaningful manual test, though US3's own tasks touch no
    US1/US2 files.
  - US4 (P4) extends US1's `home_chat_shell_page.dart` (T028) — do US1 first.
  - US5 (P5) extends US3's `session_bloc.dart` (T047) and needs US1/US2's login screen as the
    re-authentication destination — do US1 and US3 first.
- **Polish (Phase 8)**: Depends on all five user stories being complete.

### Within Each User Story

- Tests are written first and MUST fail before their matching implementation task.
- Domain entities/interfaces before use cases; use cases before blocs; blocs before pages.
- Data-layer classes (`*_remote_data_source.dart`, `*_repository_impl.dart`) before the
  `service_locator.dart` registration task that wires them in.

### Parallel Opportunities

- All Setup tasks marked [P] (T003, T004) can run in parallel once T001/T002 finish.
- Within Foundational, T005, T007, T009, T011 (and the chain T012→T013) can run in parallel; T006,
  T008, T010 each wait only on their own listed dependency.
- Within each story's test block, tasks against distinct new files are marked [P]; tasks that extend
  a file an earlier story's task already created (e.g. T031/T032/T033, T034/T035/T037/T038) are not
  marked [P] and run after that earlier task.
- US4's tasks (T051–T055) can start as soon as Foundational and US1 (for `home_chat_shell_page.dart`)
  are done, in parallel with US2/US3 work by a different contributor.

1. Complete Phase 1: Setup.
2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (blocks every story).
3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 (login → Home/Chat).

1. Setup + Foundational → foundation ready.
2. US1 (login) → test independently → demo (MVP).
3. US2 (sign-up) → test independently → demo.
4. US3 (splash/launch routing) → test independently → demo.
5. US4 (side-menu navigation) → test independently → demo.
6. US5 (session-expired overlay) → test independently → demo.
7. Phase 8 (Polish) → confirm RNF06/07/08/09 gates and run quickstart.md in full.

1. Team completes Setup + Foundational together (T001–T016).

   creates). After US1:

| Phase | Tasks | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Setup | T001–T004 | 4 |

**Parallel opportunities**: marked `[P]` wherever tasks touch distinct files (e.g., all Setup/Foundational tasks that don't share a target file, and new-file test tasks within each story); tasks that extend a file an earlier task already created are left sequential.

**Independent test per story**: each phase's "Independent Test" line states exactly how to verify that story alone (e.g., US1: submit valid credentials → land on Home/Chat).
